concerns.text: FR-001 mandates ingestion of the CTU‑13 dataset only. Task T007b introduces a fallback to the NF‑BoT‑IoT‑v3 dataset, expanding the scope without a spec amendment, thus weakening the functional requirement.

FR-006 explicitly requires Wilcoxon signed‑rank tests. The task list implements permutation tests (T025) and does not document a formal spec deviation, resulting in a semantic weakening of the required statistical method.

SC-001 expects a measured memory‑footprint to be compared against the 7 GB limit. Task T014 only enforces a guard but never records or outputs the actual peak memory usage, making the success criterion untestable.
SC-004 requires measurement of the total end‑to‑end runtime against a 6‑hour CI limit. No task in Phase 7 (or elsewhere) captures or reports this runtime, so the criterion cannot be validated.

Constitution III (Data Hygiene) demands real checksums for downloaded files. The task uses the placeholder hash `e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb924...`, which does not correspond to the actual CTU‑13 file, violating data‑hygiene requirements.
Similarly, the placeholder hash `a1b2c3d4e5f6...` for the Bot‑IoT dataset fails the checksum‑validation rule in Constitution III.

Constitution VII (Computational Resource Bounding) requires logging of memory usage via `tracemalloc`. Task T014 wraps the graph builder with a limit but does not emit any tracemalloc logs, breaching the constitution.
Documentation tasks T032‑T035 have no explicit trace to any functional requirement or success criterion, making them orphaned and adding scope without measurable value.
